reconstructed_theorem_text: For every pair of Borel probability measures μ and ν on ℝ satisfying ∫ℝ |x|² dμ(x) < ∞ and ∫ℝ |y|² dν(y) < ∞, and every 1-Lipschitz function f: ℝ → ℝ, let Π(μ,ν) be the set of couplings of μ and ν and set W₁ = inf_{γ∈Π(μ,ν)} ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} |x−y| dγ(x,y). Then, in the extended nonnegative reals, max{0, ∫ℝ f(x) dμ(x) − ∫ℝ f(y) dν(y)} ≤ W₁ and W₁ ≤ (inf_{γ∈Π(μ,ν)} ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} |x−y|² dγ(x,y))^{1/2}.
objects: The two probability measures μ and ν; the function f; joint measures γ with first marginal μ and second marginal ν; the first-power transport infimum W₁ and the square root of the squared-displacement transport infimum.
domains: μ and ν are measures on ℝ with its Borel measurable structure, f maps ℝ to ℝ, and γ is a measure on ℝ × ℝ. The difference of integrals of f is taken in ℝ; its positive part and both transport quantities are compared in the extended nonnegative reals.
quantifiers: For all μ and ν with the stated probability and moment assumptions, and for all f with the stated Lipschitz bound. Each transport infimum ranges over all couplings of that ordered pair.
assumptions: μ and ν each have total mass 1 and finite second moment. The function f satisfies |f(x) − f(y)| ≤ |x − y| for all x,y ∈ ℝ.
conclusion: The positive part of ∫ f dμ − ∫ f dν is at most W₁, and W₁ is at most the square root of the infimum of the squared-displacement integrals over couplings.
scopes: W₁ is defined locally from μ and ν and is used in both conjuncts. Clipping to zero applies to the ordered real difference as a whole; the square root applies to the whole squared-cost infimum.
constant_dependencies: The Lipschitz bound and both inequality coefficients are the universal constant 1; there are no measure- or function-dependent comparison constants. The moment and squared-cost exponent is 2.
